name: tail
description: Prints the last lines of each input file, or follows a file as it grows.

flags.description: Print the last N lines (default 10); -n +N starts at line N.
Follow: keep printing new lines as the file grows.
Like -f but also handles log rotation (retries when the file is recreated).

examples.explanation: Prints the last 50 lines of the application log.
Streams new requests as they arrive. Stop with Ctrl+C. Essential for watching live web server traffic.
Use -F when logrotate may rename and recreate the file; tail keeps following the new file.
Prints lines 100 through 120 of a large file without loading it into an editor.

about: tail -f works by tracking the file descriptor; -F re-checks the filename, surviving rotation. Combining with grep gives a live filtered feed: tail -f app.log | grep --line-buffered ERROR.
useCases: Inspect the end of large files without opening them.
Follow rotated log files reliably with -F.
mistakes: Using -f on a file that logrotate will rename — the follow goes silent; -F fixes it.
Forgetting that Ctrl+C stops the tail, not the program writing the log.
